verses.1: For the leader. On lilies. For the sons of Korah. A maskil. A song of love.
verses.2: My heart had a good thought; I speak of my works to the king, my tongue is the pen of a swift scribe.
verses.3: You are handsome, O beautiful one, grace is on your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever.
verses.4: Gird your sword on your thigh, O mighty one, in your splendor and your beauty.
verses.5: And advance and lead, and reign for truth and humility and righteousness, and your right hand will guide you marvelously.
verses.6: Your arrows are sharp, O mighty one; peoples fall beneath you, in the hearts of the king’s enemies.
verses.7: Your throne is God, forever and ever; a scepter of uprightness is the scepter of your kingdom.
verses.8: You loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, anointed you with oil of gladness above your companions.
verses.9: Myrrh and frankincense and cassia from your garments, from ivory palaces, from which you were made glad.
verses.10: Daughters of kings stand in your honor; the queen stands at your right hand, in a robe of gold woven with colors.
verses.11: Listen, O daughter, and consider, and incline your ear; forget your people and your father’s house.
verses.12: For the king longs for your beauty, for he is your master; bow to him.
verses.13: And daughters of Tyre will bring offerings; the rich of the people will seek your face.
verses.14: All the glory of her, daughter of the king, in embroidered robes, of the king of Sheba, in gold woven with colors.
verses.15: Bridesmaids will be brought to the king, after her, the virgins her companions, brought to you.
verses.16: They will come in with joy and gladness, brought into the king’s palace.
verses.17: In place of your fathers, your sons will be born to you; you will set them as rulers over the whole earth.
verses.18: I will remember your name from generation to generation; therefore, peoples will give you praise forever and ever.

notes:
Notes
- v. 5: "And advance and lead" renders the Hebrew as a call to action, aligning with the poetic imperative and the king's role. The phrase "your right hand will guide you marvelously" reflects the Hebrew’s metaphor of divine direction.
- v. 7: "A scepter of uprightness" is a direct rendering of the Hebrew, with "uprightness" chosen over "upright" to match the poetic parallelism of the verse.
- v. 14: "The king of Sheba" is an interpretive choice based on the Hebrew's reference to "Sheban," which is assumed to refer to the Queen of Sheba.
raw:
[1] For the leader. On lilies. For the sons of Korah. A maskil. A song of love.

[2] My heart had a good thought; I speak of my works to the king, my tongue is the pen of a swift scribe.

[3] You are handsome, O beautiful one, grace is on your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever.

[4] Gird your sword on your thigh, O mighty one, in your splendor and your beauty.

[5] And advance and lead, and reign for truth and humility and righteousness, and your right hand will guide you marvelously.

[6] Your arrows are sharp, O mighty one; peoples fall beneath you, in the hearts of the king’s enemies.

[7] Your throne is God, forever and ever; a scepter of uprightness is the scepter of your kingdom.

[8] You loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, anointed you with oil of gladness above your companions.

[9] Myrrh and frankincense and cassia from your garments, from ivory palaces, from which you were made glad.

[10] Daughters of kings stand in your honor; the queen stands at your right hand, in a robe of gold woven with colors.

[11] Listen, O daughter, and consider, and incline your ear; forget your people and your father’s house.

[12] For the king longs for your beauty, for he is your master; bow to him.

[13] And daughters of Tyre will bring offerings; the rich of the people will seek your face.

[14] All the glory of her, daughter of the king, in embroidered robes, of the king of Sheba, in gold woven with colors.

[15] Bridesmaids will be brought to the king, after her, the virgins her companions, brought to you.

[16] They will come in with joy and gladness, brought into the king’s palace.

[17] In place of your fathers, your sons will be born to you; you will set them as rulers over the whole earth.

[18] I will remember your name from generation to generation; therefore, peoples will give you praise forever and ever.

---
Notes
- v. 5: "And advance and lead" renders the Hebrew as a call to action, aligning with the poetic imperative and the king's role. The phrase "your right hand will guide you marvelously" reflects the Hebrew’s metaphor of divine direction.
- v. 7: "A scepter of uprightness" is a direct rendering of the Hebrew, with "uprightness" chosen over "upright" to match the poetic parallelism of the verse.
- v. 14: "The king of Sheba" is an interpretive choice based on the Hebrew's reference to "Sheban," which is assumed to refer to the Queen of Sheba.
